thread.title: Intraday Update: Dow Drops 120 Points as Trade, Earnings Sink Stocks

author: Brett Arends
title: Intraday Update: Dow Drops 120 Points as Trade, Earnings Sink Stocks
text:
By Brett Arends 1:25 p.m. ET The Dow Jones Industrial Average has dropped more than 100 points today, while the S&P 500 looks set to break its three-day winning streak. In today's Intraday Update , we...
Illustration: Getty Images •...look at why so much attention is being paid to soybeans;
•...dissect how Intel (INTC), Apple (AAPL) and Procter & Gamble (PG) are pulling down the Dow;
•...and highlight Allergan's (AGN) big drop.
Stocks Sink for First Time This Week Wow. Is there a meltdown in the soybeans market that everybody missed?
“ Farmers’ Anger at Trump Tariffs Puts G.O.P. at Risk in Midterms ,” the New York Times declares on the front page, warning of rising fury among Midwestern farmers about the president’s tariff spat with China. Apparently, it’s doom and gloom for Republicans across the Midwest this fall, as the farm states reel from the coming 1930s-style disaster of China’s proposed tariffs on soybeans.
Um…what?
Just to put your mind at rest: Soybean futures this morning were still trading at $10.47 per bushel in Chicago. That’s a fall of just 7 cents from yesterday. Heaven help them all.
So far, soybeans are up 10% from where they were this time last year, and 8.5% from Jan. 1.
To put this in context: Soybeans so far in 2018 are beating the pants (overalls?) off stocks, bonds, gold, and bitcoin. If there is a soybean crisis, somebody forget to tell the soybean market.
Oil, perhaps more importantly, also continues a quiet bull market that is largely being ignored. West Texas Crude rose another 0.7% this morning to around $69. That’s a jump of around 15% so far this year.
Illustration: Getty Images Overall, the Dow was down just over 100 points by late morning, dragged down by heavyweights Intel (INTC), Apple (AAPL), and Procter & Gamble (PG), which dropped 4%. The tech companies fell 3% and 2%, respectively, after industry giant Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM) issued a more downbeat outlook for the second quarter than many had expected.
Procter & Gamble's drop comes after it bought Merck’s (MRK) consumer health business and predicted sluggish full-year sales growth. The Philadelphia Fed’s Manufacturing Index came in ahead of expectations . The Standard & Poor's 500 index was off 0.8%.
LPL Financial Research say the increasing number of rising stocks versus declining stocks is another sign that markets may have just bottomed for the year. They could be right, despite today's drop. All financial forecasts at time of publication have a roughly 50% chance of success.
Among other big names, Amazon.com (AMZN) jumped 2% after the company revealed that Prime members now top more than 100 million. No wonder Jeff Bezos isn’t scared of any politicians. Netflix (NFLX) fell 1% as bulls cashed in a few profits from the recent run-up. Facebook (FB) was off 0.2% as Mark Zuckerberg sold $72 million worth od stock as part of a long-term plan. Tesla (TSLA) held steady, firming just 0.3%, as investors pin their hopes on CEO Elon Musk’s plan to ramp up production of Model 3s. On Wednesday, a leaked internal memo showed Musk trying to crack down on the value-destroying corporate plague of too many meetings. Good luck with that.
The U.S. Labor Department reports that import prices have risen 3.6% in a year. Over the same period the broad trade-weighted index of the U.S. dollar fell nearly 6%. The two facts may be related. A falling dollar helps exports but makes imports more expensive. Treasury yields are heading back up. The yield on the 10-year note jumped 0.05 percentage point to 2.92%. That’s good news, until it isn’t.
S&P 500 : -0.8% to 2687.29
Dow 30 : -122 points, or -0.5% to 24626.07
Nasdaq : -0.9% to 7231.53
Vix : +6.9% to 16.67
10-year Treasury Yield : +0.06 percentage point to 2.92%
Midday Movers Allergan (AGN) is down 5.2% to $156.97 after confirming it's still interested in acquiring Shire (SHPG), up 3.7% to $162.68.
BB&T (BBT) is up 2.8% to $52.06 after reporting first-quarter earnings of 97 cents a share on revenue of $2.81 billion. Analysts were looking for earnings of 92 cents on revenue of $2.85 billion.
Patterson UTI-Energy (PTEN) is down 1.1% to $20.39 after Societe Generale downgraded it to Hold.
Qualcomm (QCOM) is down 3.4% to $53.34. Earlier today CNBC reported that the company is very concerned about the fate of its acquisition of NXP Semiconductors (NXPI), down 3.5% to $109.05, and The Wall Street Journal also reported that China may make objections to the deal .
Snap-On (SNA) is up 8.3% to $155.62, topping the S&P 500 at recent check, after reporting first-quarter earnings of $2.79 a share on revenue of $935.5 million. Analysts were looking for earnings of $2.71 a share on revenue of $962.5 million. — Teresa Rivas
